findings.text: Opening a terminal instance binds the indexed port structure to the caller, rejects a dead service processor, records the terminal, updates the open count under the port lock, resets the outbound sequence, enables receive interrupts, then for non console ports performs a version handshake and raises the data terminal ready indication while console ports return immediately as already handshaked.

Closing lowers the open count under lock and when the last opener exits discards partial input and, except for console ports, disables interrupts, marks closed and closing, waits for in flight interrupt handlers, drains pending output with a bounded wait plus worker cancellation, asks the peer to stop, and discards trailing input; hangup detaches the terminal and resets count and pending output; flush waits for empty then cancels background work and drops any remainder.

Transmit path stages caller bytes into a fixed size per port buffer while room remains, attempts immediate emission after each chunk, schedules delayed background pushes when data remains, reports free and occupied space through room and occupancy queries, and uses a worker that requeues slowly while not open and otherwise pushes then wakes empty waiters and the line discipline after draining.

Link setup discards stale inbound bytes, enters a wait for version response state, issues a version query, then blocks until the open state is reached; a background worker retries this sequence and reports permanent console loss; fatal output errors move the link to a dead state that causes later opens to fail, while orderly close moves a non console link to closed.

Each outbound control or data packet carries an incremented sequence value rendered big endian and a length covering header plus payload; modem control handling only observes and modifies the data terminal ready bit under a mask, with set failing the whole operation when the lower transport accepts fewer bytes than offered and get refreshing a cached copy before reporting.

Flow control operations disable receive signaling when throttled and on unthrottle emit an overflow indication if throttling was active, push received data upward, then re enable signaling; modem queries refresh state and updates are restricted to the data terminal ready bit with an unchanged fast path; a static operations table exposes terminal open and close, transmit and flow control, occupancy queries, hangup, and modem methods to the terminal layer.

Early initialization scans the device tree for compatible serial nodes, reads terminal number and interrupt specifiers, caps the population, initializes per port work queues locks and ports with closed state and empty input, maps interrupts, and registers a console when ports exist; later driver setup allocates a raw system terminal driver with fixed name major minor and low speed character defaults, links each port, requests its interrupt, switches the state wait helper from polling to interrupt driven, and on registration failure restores polling and releases resources.

Console printing is skipped unless the link is open and otherwise expands each line feed into carriage return plus line feed within a bounded staging area, emitting full chunks through the data packet path and discarding a chunk that reports an error; device lookup returns the registered driver and index while setup validates the index, issues a close to allow rate renegotiation, handshakes, raises data terminal ready, and marks the port as console with buffered printing enabled.

Shared interrupt bookkeeping uses a hash entry holding a hash linkage, numeric interrupt identity, a spin lock guarding the chain membership but not the hash itself, and a head pointer to the chained port list; the hash uses a narrow width and interrupt dispatch is bounded to avoid unbounded looping on a busy shared line.

The interrupt hash is protected by a dedicated mutex during lookup creation unlink and teardown while each hash entry has its own interrupt saving spin lock for chain splice operations; handler iteration holds the entry lock for the whole sweep; hypervisor terminal ports serialize open count modem state output accounting throttle flags and state transitions with a per port interrupt saving spin lock, with close dropping the lock across interrupt synchronization and output drain before reacquiring.

Chain membership is created on demand under the hash mutex with allocation failure reported as out of memory, linked at the head or as a new isolated entry, then bound to the interrupt line with automatic unlink on request failure; removal warns on missing entries or empty heads, releases the interrupt only when the last member leaves, deletes the hash node and frees the entry when the chain becomes empty, and adjusts the head when the initial member departs.

Timer helpers provide polled operation: a simple helper invokes the port handler then rearms after a fifo derived poll interval, while a backup variant masks device interrupts, samples interrupt identity and line status, synthesizes a transmit indication when transmit is enabled with pending bytes and an empty holding register despite an idle indication, emits pending characters, restores the mask, and rearms with an added delay; the poll interval itself is a fraction of the fifo drain time minus a small margin with a tiny floor and the fifo time adds slop.

Port locking combines interrupt saving spin operations with optional non blocking console acquisition that spins until the console context is acquired and later releases it; console use is recognized only when the port has an attached registered console indexed to the same line with non blocking flags and an atomic writer, with the registration and flag checks performed under the already held port lock.

Risky behaviors include stale input drain bounded only by timeout, silent discard of unsent output after flush timeout, slow retry while the peer is dead versus brief requeue while congested, permanent console loss reported but not retried, invalid open count indicating unbalanced close, fatal peer death inferred from an output error, and shared interrupt teardown that must free the line exactly when the chain empties while warning on inconsistent hash state.

The terminal operations table and console descriptor along with the shared interrupt handler and chain link helpers form the outward interfaces through which the generic terminal, console, and interrupt layers drive these drivers.

Sharing uses a pass ceiling of 512 [CITED] and a hash width of 5 [CITED] bits; fifo timing adds 20 [CITED] milliseconds of slop with a floor of 1 [CITED] tick, poll timing uses a threshold of 6 [CITED] with roughly half [CITED] minus 2 [CITED] and a floor of 1 [CITED], and backup polling adds an extra 1 [CITED] second divided by 5 [CITED].

Terminal defaults use 9600 [CITED] baud for input and output with 8 [CITED] bit characters; close signaling uses a length of 6 [CITED]; background retransmit waits 10 [CITED] ticks while congested and 1 [CITED] second while not open.
A static transmit test skip flag is declared without further use shown in these fragments.
